subject: Chemistry
title: Chemical Kinetics
summary: Chemical kinetics is about how fast reactions go. Rate = change in concentration per unit time, divided by the stoichiometric coefficient so that it is the same for every species.
The rate law (rate = k[A]ˣ[B]ʸ) is found by experiment. The order (x + y) can be 0, fractional or whole; molecularity applies only to elementary steps and is always a whole number.
Integrated rate laws: zero order [A] = [A]₀ − kt (t½ ∝ [A]₀); first order ln([A]₀/[A]) = kt (t½ = 0.693/k, independent of concentration).
Rates rise sharply with temperature (Arrhenius: k = Ae^(−Ea/RT)) because more molecules have energy above Ea. Catalysts lower Ea without changing ΔH or equilibrium.

formulas.name: Rate of reaction
formulas.formula: for aA + bB → cC + dD:  rate = −(1/a)d[A]/dt = −(1/b)d[B]/dt = (1/c)d[C]/dt
formulas.note: Divide by the coefficient — the rate of disappearance of A is a × rate.

formulas.name: Rate law
formulas.mistake: x and y come from experiment, not from the balanced equation.

formulas.name: Units of k
formulas.formula: (mol L⁻¹)¹⁻ⁿ s⁻¹:  zero order mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹;  first s⁻¹;  second L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹

formulas.name: Zero-order reaction
formulas.when: Reactions on saturated catalyst surfaces, photochemical reactions.
formulas.note: t½ increases with initial concentration for zero order.

formulas.name: First-order reaction
formulas.mistake: t½ of a first-order reaction does not depend on initial concentration.

formulas.name: First-order shortcuts
formulas.formula: t₇₅% = 2 t½;  t₈₇.₅% = 3 t½;  t₉₉.₉% ≈ 10 t½;  t₉₉% = 2 t₉₀%

formulas.name: Pseudo-first-order
formulas.formula: a second-order reaction with one reactant in large excess behaves as first order
formulas.when: Acid hydrolysis of esters, inversion of cane sugar.

formulas.name: Arrhenius equation
formulas.note: Use kelvin, and R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ with Ea in joules.

formulas.name: Collision theory
formulas.formula: rate = Z_AB e^(−Ea/RT) × P  (P = steric/orientation factor)

topics.title: Average and instantaneous rate
topics.explain: Average rate = Δ[R]/Δt over an interval; instantaneous rate = slope of the concentration–time curve at a point. Rate usually decreases as reactants are used up.

topics.title: Factors affecting rate
topics.explain: Concentration (or pressure), temperature, catalyst, surface area of solids, and light for photochemical reactions.

topics.title: Order vs molecularity
topics.explain: Order is experimental, can be zero or fractional, and refers to the overall reaction. Molecularity is theoretical, a whole number (1, 2, rarely 3) and defined only for elementary steps. For complex reactions the slowest step decides the rate law.

topics.title: Graphs to identify order
topics.explain: Zero order: [A] vs t is a straight line (slope −k). First order: ln[A] (or log[A]) vs t is a straight line (slope −k or −k/2.303). Rate vs [A] is flat for zero order and a straight line through the origin for first order.

topics.title: Activation energy and catalysts
topics.explain: Only colliding molecules with energy ≥ Ea and the right orientation react. A catalyst provides a new path with lower Ea, speeds up forward and backward reactions equally, is not used up, and does not change ΔH, ΔG or K.

topics.title: Effect of temperature (Maxwell distribution)
topics.explain: Raising T shifts the energy distribution so the fraction of molecules above Ea (the area beyond Ea) roughly doubles for every 10 K. ln k vs 1/T is a straight line with slope −Ea/R and intercept ln A.

ratta: k = Ae^(−Ea/RT);  slope of ln k vs 1/T = −Ea/R.
Catalyst lowers Ea; no change in ΔH or K.
